title: The 95% interval for a difference of 9.0 mg/dL, standard error 4.13
alt: Bell curve centred on a difference of 9.0 mg/dL with the region from 0.9 to 17.1 shaded, and a marked line at 0 sitting outside the shading.
longDescription: The curve is centred on the observed difference of 9.0 mg/dL and has a standard deviation of 4.13 mg/dL, which is the standard error of that difference. It shows how far apart repeat estimates would land if this study were run again and again on the same 30-and-30 design. The shaded band runs from 0.9 to 17.1 mg/dL and covers the middle 95% of the curve, which is the observed difference plus and minus 1.96 standard errors. That band is the 95% confidence interval, and it is 16.2 mg/dL wide. Two vertical lines are marked. One sits at 9.0 mg/dL, the observed difference and the centre of the curve. The other sits at 0 mg/dL, the value that would mean no difference between the two groups. The line at 0 is outside the shaded band, about 2.2 standard errors below the centre, but only just: the band's lower edge sits 0.9 mg/dL above it, which is about a fifth of one standard error. Read the curve as a picture of where repeat estimates would fall, not as a picture of where the true difference lies.

xAxis.label: Difference in fasting glucose, late group minus early group

yAxis.label: Relative frequency of a repeat estimate

series.label: Where a repeat of this study would land
